skill.name: browser-task-and-automation-and-delegation
skill.description: Delegates browser automation tasks to a Chrome DevTools expert agent for navigation, form interaction, screenshots, performance analysis, testing, data extraction, and network simulation.
skill.summary: Delegate browser automation to a Chrome DevTools agent while keeping main chat context concise.

security_audit.summary: All static command-execution findings are Markdown backticks or fenced examples, not executable Ruby or shell code. The hardcoded URLs are example.com placeholders, and the entropy alert is explained by readable Chinese Markdown. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Ambiguous code fences triggered command-execution scanning.
remediation.suggestion: Mark examples as plain text and avoid standalone triple backticks around tool parameters when possible.
Label credentials as dummy values and advise users never to place real passwords in reusable prompts.

remediation.issue: Browser automation includes data extraction and authenticated workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit consent and scope guidance for private pages, scraping, screenshots, and network monitoring.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Tasks with Delegated DevTools
content.value_statement: Browser work can flood the main chat with page state, screenshots, and request logs. This skill delegates those tasks to a Chrome DevTools agent and returns concise results.
actual_capabilities: Delegates browser work to a chrome-devtools-expert agent through the Task tool.
Opens pages, navigates tabs, and waits for page load states.
Clicks elements, fills forms, selects options, and submits workflows.
Captures full-page or element screenshots and page text snapshots.
Runs performance traces and reports Core Web Vitals findings.
Extracts page data with JavaScript and monitors network requests.
limitations: Requires a configured Chrome DevTools MCP server and the named subagent.
Does not bypass authentication, paywalls, captchas, or site access controls.
Can expose sensitive page data if used on private sessions.
Example credentials are placeholders and should not be reused.

use_cases.title: Check a Web Flow
use_cases.description: Run browser steps, verify visible states, capture screenshots, and report whether the workflow behaves as expected.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Page Performance
use_cases.description: Collect loading metrics, console errors, network observations, and Core Web Vitals for a target page.

use_cases.title: Collect Page Evidence
use_cases.description: Open specified pages, extract visible information, and return a concise summary with source page context.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Page Screenshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the target URL, wait for the page to finish loading, capture a full-page screenshot, and summarize the visible page title.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Form Submission
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the current page to fill the specified form fields, submit the form, wait for the response, and report success or failure.

prompt_templates.title: Measure Page Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the target URL, run a performance trace during reload, capture Core Web Vitals, and list the largest bottlenecks.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Multi-Step Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate through the requested pages, perform each browser action in order, collect screenshots or metrics, and return only key findings.

output_examples.input: Open a product page and capture a screenshot.
output_examples.output: The agent loaded the page, saved a full-page screenshot, and reported the product title and visible page status.

output_examples.input: Analyze a landing page under slow network conditions.
output_examples.output: The agent simulated slow network speed, measured loading behavior, restored normal settings, and summarized the most important delays.

output_examples.input: Extract all visible article titles from the current page.
output_examples.output: The agent collected the visible titles, removed duplicates, and returned a short list with the page context.

best_practices: Use specific URLs and expected outcomes so the delegated agent can stop quickly.
Request summaries of only important page state, errors, screenshots, or measurements.
Confirm permission before using authenticated pages or collecting page data.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to bypass login, paywalls, captchas, or site rules.
Sending real passwords or private tokens in reusable prompt examples.
Asking for broad crawling without scope, rate limits, or data minimization.

faq.question: What does this skill delegate?
faq.answer: It delegates browser navigation, page interaction, screenshots, performance checks, testing, data extraction, and network simulation.

faq.question: Does it run browser work in the main chat?
faq.answer: No. It routes browser work to a chrome-devtools-expert agent and asks that agent to return concise results.

faq.question: Which tools does it depend on?
faq.answer: It expects a Chrome DevTools MCP setup and access to the named browser automation subagent.

faq.question: Can it interact with private pages?
faq.answer: Only when the user has permission and provides clear scope. Sensitive page data should be minimized.

faq.question: Can it perform scraping?
faq.answer: It can extract page information, but users should respect site rules, privacy limits, and rate limits.

faq.question: Is it useful for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
